question.worked_solution:
We recognize that the series looks similar to the Maclaurin expansion for $f(x)=\operatorname{sin}⁡x.$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡x & =x-\frac{{x}^{3}}{3!}+\frac{{x}^{5}}{5!}-⋯+\frac{(-1)^{n}{x}^{2n+1}}{(2n+1)!}+⋯\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $x=\frac{\pi }{4}$ into our Maclaurin expansion gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =\frac{\pi }{4}-\frac{(\pi /4)^{3}}{3!}+\frac{(\pi /4)^{5}}{5!}-\frac{(\pi /4)^{7}}{7!}+⋯+\frac{(-1)^{n}(\pi /4)^{2n+1}}{(2n+1)!}+⋯ \\ \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} & =\frac{\pi }{4}-\frac{(\pi /4)^{3}}{3!}+\frac{(\pi /4)^{5}}{5!}-\frac{(\pi /4)^{7}}{7!}+⋯+\frac{(-1)^{n}(\pi /4)^{2n+1}}{(2n+1)!}+⋯\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the sum of the series is $\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}.$
